newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end sharply up on land liquidity plan.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end sharply up on land liquidity plan.

text.p: Tokyo's key Nikkei stock average closed over two percent higher on Tuesday, as market participants rejoiced over the government's decision to draw up plans to boost the stagnant land market by the end of the month which is also the end of the fiscal year, brokers said.
The 225-share Nikkei average gained 391.70 points, or 2.17 percent, to 18,445.20. Its June futures jumped 340 points to 18,400.

"Futures-linked buying, mostly by dealers, was ignited by the finance minister's comments in the morning expressing plans to improve land liquidity and that set the pace for the rest of the day," Kenji Karikome of Daiwa Securities said.
Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference that measures to improve land liquidity would be drawn up by the government by March 31.
